exactMemory.name: Exact Memory
exactMemory.summary: A perfect ledger of every value and how often it appeared.
exactMemory.help: Stores each distinct value with a counter, so every answer is exact until the table fills. Once full it refuses new values and widens its bounds by how many it turned away. It costs 64 bits per distinct value, so it only suits small streams.
exactMemory.flavor: Never forgets a face, but runs out of pages.

reservoirSampling.name: Reservoir Sampling
reservoirSampling.summary: A fair random sample of the stream, shown as raw values.
reservoirSampling.help: Keeps a uniform random sample and scales it up to estimate counts, so it can answer any question roughly and shows the raw values it holds. It cannot see deletes, so deleted values linger in the sample as ghosts.
reservoirSampling.flavor: A handful of witnesses, chosen without favorites.

bloomFilter.name: Bloom Filter

knob.name: expected items
knob.description: How many distinct values you expect to insert. It sets how many bits each value uses.

bloomFilter.summary: Answers whether a value has appeared, in very little space.
bloomFilter.help: A bit array where each value sets several bits. It never misses a value that was inserted, but it can flag one that was not, and the false alarms grow as it fills. It cannot delete, so deleted values stay flagged.
bloomFilter.flavor: Certain when it says no. Merely hopeful when it says yes.

countMinSketch.name: Count-Min Sketch

knob.name: depth
knob.description: The number of counter rows. More rows make a bad overestimate less likely.

countMinSketch.summary: Estimates how often a value appeared, in a small grid of counters.
countMinSketch.help: A grid of counters with one row per hash. A query takes the smallest counter across the rows, so it never underestimates a value but can overshoot when counters are shared. It handles deletes.
countMinSketch.flavor: Counts by crowd noise, and takes the quietest reading.

logLog.name: LogLog
logLog.summary: Estimates how many distinct values appeared, using almost no space.
logLog.help: Each register remembers the rarest hash pattern it has seen, which reveals roughly how many distinct values have passed. It is accurate on large streams, biased on small ones, and it ignores deletes.
logLog.flavor: Judges a crowd by its rarest face.

linearCounting.name: Linear Counting
linearCounting.summary: Estimates distinct values from the share of empty bits in a bitmap.
linearCounting.help: Each value sets one bit, and the fraction still empty reveals how many distinct values there were. It is precise while the bitmap has room, but once every bit is set it can only say at least this many. It ignores deletes.
linearCounting.flavor: Counts the guests by the empty chairs.

hyperLogLog.name: HyperLogLog
hyperLogLog.summary: Estimates how many distinct values appeared, accurately from tiny streams to huge ones.
hyperLogLog.help: Like LogLog, each register remembers the rarest hash pattern it has seen, but it averages them harmonically, which tames the odd register that got lucky. While many registers are still empty it counts those instead, as Linear Counting does. Its error is about 1.04 divided by the square root of the register count. It is made by fusing LogLog with Linear Counting at a rest stop; in real life that is a teaching shortcut, since HyperLogLog's main change from LogLog is the harmonic mean. It ignores deletes.
hyperLogLog.flavor: Counts the crowd by its rarest faces, and by the empty seats.

countSketch.name: Count Sketch

knob.name: depth
knob.description: The number of counter rows. More rows make a bad estimate less likely; an odd number works best.

countSketch.summary: Estimates how often a value appeared, without leaning high or low.
countSketch.help: A grid of signed counters: each value adds or subtracts one in every row, with a sign of its own in that row, so other values' collisions cancel out on average. A query takes the median over the rows. Unlike Count-Min it can answer below the truth as well as above it, so strike on its upper bound when a miss would hurt. Its error follows the size of the whole stream's heavy values, not its length, so it beats Count-Min when a few values dominate and handles deletes exactly.
countSketch.flavor: Counts by listening for the echoes that cancel out.

topKTracker.name: Top-K Tracker

knob.name: depth
knob.description: The number of counter rows in its Count-Min grid.

topKTracker.summary: Tracks the heaviest values exactly, and the rest roughly.
topKTracker.help: A Count-Min grid ranks the values and a short list keeps an interval around the heaviest ones, which then moves by exactly one for each insert or delete. A value that joined the list early keeps a narrow interval however big the stream grows, so on a skewed stream the heavy values are answered far better than the grid alone could. The rest are answered by the grid. A quarter of its Space holds the list. It is made by fusing Count-Min Sketch with Exact Memory at a rest stop.
topKTracker.flavor: Remembers the loudest voices, and shrugs at the crowd.

cuckooFilter.name: Cuckoo Filter

knob.name: fingerprint
knob.description: Bits in each stored fingerprint. More bits mean fewer false alarms but fewer places to store them.

cuckooFilter.summary: Flags values it has seen, and can forget the ones deleted.
cuckooFilter.help: Stores a short fingerprint of every value in one of two buckets, and shuffles fingerprints between their two buckets to make room. A value is flagged when its fingerprint is in either bucket, so a stranger is flagged by chance, about 8 times in 2 to the power of the fingerprint bits when it is full. Unlike a Bloom Filter it handles deletes, but once it is more than about 95 percent full it starts dropping fingerprints, which hides real values: false negatives. Its range allows for both.
cuckooFilter.flavor: Tucks every face into one of two drawers, and shuffles when both are full.

kMinimumValues.name: K-Minimum Values
kMinimumValues.summary: Estimates how many distinct values appeared, from the k smallest hashes.
kMinimumValues.help: Keeps the k smallest hashes of the distinct values it has seen. While it has fewer than k it counts them exactly. Past that, the k-th smallest hash says how crowded the values are: the estimate is k minus 1 over that hash as a share of the range, with an error of about 1 over the square root of k minus 2. It ignores deletes, like LogLog, so a deleted value still counts until the range allows for it, and two sketches merge into the sketch of both streams.
kMinimumValues.flavor: Counts the crowd by how close its nearest strangers stand.

kllSketch.name: KLL Sketch
kllSketch.summary: Estimates where a value ranks among everything that appeared, to within a couple of percent.
kllSketch.help: Keeps a few dozen sorted samples in levels. When a level fills, it keeps every second item and promotes them to the level above, where each one stands for twice as many units. The rank it reports is off by about 1.6 over its k, the same at every quantile, and it knows how far off it can be. It ignores deletes, which remove units at random and so only add noise. Ask it for a quantile, then strike with its upper end to be sure of reaching the armor.
kllSketch.flavor: Keeps one voice in two, and lets each stand for the crowd it left behind.

tDigest.name: t-digest
tDigest.summary: Estimates where a value ranks, sharpest at the extremes: the 1st and 99th percentiles.
tDigest.help: Keeps weighted centroids, each the mean of the values it stands for. A centroid may cover many units in the middle of the distribution but only a few at either end, so the tails are tracked closely and the middle more coarsely. The smallest and largest values are kept exactly. It ignores deletes, which remove units at random and so only add noise. For a 99th percentile armor it beats a KLL Sketch of the same Space; for the median they are close.
tDigest.flavor: Averages the crowd into a few voices, and keeps the loudest and quietest exactly.

minHash.name: MinHash
minHash.summary: Tells which sets of values are close copies of the stream, by comparing short signatures.
minHash.help: Keeps, for each of many hash functions, the smallest hash of any value it has seen. Two sets agree on that minimum with exactly the chance of their Jaccard similarity (shared values over values in either), so the share of agreeing slots estimates it, within about 1 over twice the square root of the slots. It flags the copies at or above the threshold, and says how many of the flagged ones are surely real. It ignores deletes, so ghosts (deleted values) still count in its set, which widens its range under Churn.
minHash.flavor: Knows a face by the first thing it would pick out of a crowd.

scalableBloom.name: Scalable Bloom Filter
scalableBloom.summary: A stack of Bloom filters that adds a larger, tighter layer whenever one fills, so a stream that grows past the plan does not flood it.
scalableBloom.help: Starts with one layer in a quarter of the Space and keeps the rest in reserve. When a layer holds as many values as it was sized for, a new layer twice the size and half as likely to flag a stranger is added, and a value is present if any layer says so, so the false-positive rates add up to a bound that holds as the stream grows. The reserve is finite: once it is spent the last layer fills like any Bloom filter. A Bloom filter sized right for the stream beats it; it is for when you do not know the size. It cannot delete.
scalableBloom.flavor: Never says the room is full; just builds another one.

spectralBloom.name: Spectral Bloom Filter

knob.name: expected items
knob.description: How many different values you expect; it sets how many counters each value uses.

spectralBloom.summary: A Bloom filter made of counters: Presence and Frequency from one slot, and it handles deletes.
spectralBloom.help: Every value adds one to each of its counters, and a delete takes one off. Presence asks whether all of a value's counters are above zero; Frequency reads the smallest, which is never below the truth, so strike on it. The counters are 16 bits each, so the same Space buys half as many cells as a Count-Min Sketch of 32-bit counters, and a counter that reaches its top stops and says only "at least".
spectralBloom.flavor: A Bloom filter that learned to count.

dyadicCountMin.name: Dyadic Count-Min

knob.name: depth
knob.description: The number of counter rows in each sketch. More rows make a bad overestimate less likely.

dyadicCountMin.summary: Finds quantiles from Count-Min sketches over the value range's runs, in 256 buckets.
dyadicCountMin.help: Cuts each value to its top 8 bits, giving 256 ordered buckets, and counts every aligned run of buckets (the whole range, its halves, quarters and so on). A quantile is found by walking down, going left when the target falls in the left half. The few big runs are counted exactly; the small ones are Count-Min sketches that share the rest of the Space, and they only overcount, so it finds a bucket at or below the true one. It answers with a bucket's edges, and says the quantile has no upper end when its error reaches past the total. It handles deletes. It needs a lot of Space for a tight answer: a KLL Sketch is far sharper at the same size.
dyadicCountMin.flavor: Halves the range again and again until the crowd is found.

quotientFilter.name: Quotient Filter

knob.name: remainder bits
knob.description: How many bits of each value's fingerprint are stored in its slot. More bits make a false alarm rarer and each slot dearer.

quotientFilter.summary: A compact table of fingerprints that handles deletes and merges.
quotientFilter.help: Splits a hash into a quotient, which picks a home slot, and a remainder, which the slot stores, with three bits of bookkeeping that let neighbours that share a home push each other along. The table has as many slots as fit (a power of two), each remainder bits plus three. A value is present if its fingerprint is held, so a stranger is flagged about as often as the load times two to the minus the remainder bits. A delete takes away one copy exactly, and two filters of the same shape merge. Every insert takes a slot, repeats too, and a full table drops the next one and so hides a value.
quotientFilter.flavor: Files each face under its first letters, and makes room when two share a drawer.

simHash.name: SimHash
simHash.summary: Judges how alike two sets are from the angle between them, read off a fingerprint of signs.
simHash.help: Gives every value a random sign on each of many planes and keeps a counter of the signs it has seen. A copy gets its own signs the same way, and the share of planes where the two disagree estimates their angle; the cosine of the angle, with the sizes of the two sets, gives the similarity. It is rough: a plane says less than a MinHash slot, and it is weak on duplicates, because a value that repeats outweighs the others, so on a stream with a few very common values it sees the copies as less like the stream than they are. It ignores deletes.
simHash.flavor: Does not look at the faces, only at which way the crowd leans.

lsh.name: Locality-Sensitive Hashing
lsh.summary: A MinHash that flags every copy that could be real: it almost never misses one, and lets look-alikes close to the line through.
lsh.help: Keeps MinHash's minima and cuts them into bands of several rows. A copy is flagged when, in some band, every row agrees with the stream's. The number of rows is the most for which a copy right at the threshold is still flagged nine times in ten, so a real copy is almost never missed, but a look-alike just under the line is flagged more often than not. It tells you how many of the flagged are surely real, as MinHash does. Strike on all it flags when a miss costs more than a wrong flag; otherwise a MinHash is the better judge.
lsh.flavor: Throws a wide net, and trusts you to sort the catch.

hyperMinHash.name: HyperMinHash
hyperMinHash.summary: MinHash laid out like a HyperLogLog: about four times as many registers for the same Space.
hyperMinHash.help: Each value goes to one bucket, as in HyperLogLog, and a register keeps the smallest hash of its bucket in a small coded form (where its first one bit is and the next three bits), eight bits in all. So the same Space holds four times as many registers as a MinHash has slots, and an insert touches one. Two sets agree in a bucket when the union's smallest hash is in both, which has the chance of their Jaccard similarity, or when two different ones happen to have the same code, which it measures with a set of the copy's size from outside the stream and takes out. It ignores deletes, and the same registers count the distinct values.
hyperMinHash.flavor: Remembers a fingerprint of the first thing it would pick, in a single byte.

thetaSketch.name: Theta Sketch
thetaSketch.summary: K-Minimum Values that merge by themselves: counts the union of two enemies' streams.
thetaSketch.help: Keeps the k smallest hashes of the distinct values it has seen, like K-Minimum Values; the largest of them, as a share of the hash range, is its theta, and every value below theta is in the sketch. Two of them (one watching each enemy in a two-enemy fight) take the k smallest of both and so count the union, with no Merge enchantment. Alone it counts as K-Minimum Values does, with the same error and the same blindness to deletes.
thetaSketch.flavor: Two small mirrors, put together, show the whole crowd.
